title: SQL Injection via String Interpolation in Queries
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x; database adapters and query interfaces (database drivers, ActiveRecord-style fragment APIs) parameterize bound values but interpolate SQL fragments verbatim
security_mechanism: Query interfaces accept both bound values and raw SQL fragments; inside a fragment, #{} is evaluated by Ruby before the database sees the string, so a quote or SQL keyword in the value becomes statement structure. Identifier and keyword positions (ORDER BY column, GROUP BY, limit/offset fragments) cannot be parameterized at all, so code routinely interpolates sort keys and column names there even when values elsewhere are bound — making sort/filter parameters the usual injection point. Placeholders (? or named binds) hand values to the adapter out-of-band, so bound values cannot alter the parse.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters for search terms, sort keys, filter fields, column names and pagination values that reach fragment construction.
source_sink_clues.sink: Condition/fragment APIs taking interpolated strings (where("... #{...}"), order("... #{...}")), and raw driver execute calls built by concatenation

tracking_guards: Require placeholders for every value; require identifier parts to be resolved through a fixed allowlist hash mapping client keys to column names (or the adapter's identifier quoting); require Integer() casting for limit/offset before interpolation.
not_candidate_when: Values are bound through placeholders, interpolated identifier parts come from a fixed server-side allowlist, or numeric fields are cast with Integer() before reaching the fragment.
public_references: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html
OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
